To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Facebook is used by people to connect with friends, to keep up with what they are doing, to look at them and to look up at them, and to share content.
Facebook users are motivated by social connection, shared identity and the desire to be informed, and that these motivations are associated with different demographic characteristics and site use.
people use Facebook to look at, look up or keep up with people.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how people use Facebook, and the motives that drive those uses.
the social and cultural aspects of Facebook and the uses and gratifications that users derive from the site.
the ways in which people use Facebook, and the reasons why they do so, as well as the implications for their privacy and the privacy settings they employ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
people use Facebook for a variety of reasons, including social connection, content, social network surfing, social investigation and self-presentation.
the uses and gratifications theory is an important theory that can be used to explain the uses of social media and the reasons behind those uses.
people use facebook for a variety of reasons and the uses and gratifications they get out of it vary from one individual to the other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Facebook is not just a tool for keeping up with friends, but also a tool for looking up and looking for friends.

Facebook users are using the site to keep up with people, to look up people, and to look up themselves, and that they are doing so for different reasons and in different ways depending upon their demographic characteristics.
people who use Facebook to connect with others and to share their identities are more likely to visit the site more frequently, and are more likely to have their privacy settings set to public.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Facebook users are motivated to use the site for a variety of reasons.
Facebook use and gratifications are not uniform.
users have different motivations and uses of Facebook, and these uses are related to different gratifications and privacy settings.
